## What to Look For in a Dispensary POS System


A dispensary POS system should be judged on seven criteria: compliance automation, reliability and uptime, total cost, speed on the floor, all-in-one scope, support model, and data ownership. The first three are deal-breakers. A platform that fails any one of them comes off the list before you compare anything else.


If you're still mapping the category, start with[What is Cannabis POS Software?](https://getmeadow.com/blog/what-is-cannabis-pos-software) and come back.


### 1. Compliance Automation


Compliance automation means the POS reports sales and inventory to your state's track-and-trace system automatically and catches errors before the state sees them. Manual CSV uploads and nightly reconciliation are a tax on your time and an audit risk. Ask every vendor:


- Does the system report to Metrc in real time or in an end-of-day batch, and which does your state require?
- What has to happen inside Metrc versus inside the POS to stay compliant?
- What stops a package from being oversold or going negative?
- How quickly did the last state rule change, such as a new excise tax calculation, show up in the software?


💡 **How Meadow handles this:** Meadow reports to Metrc automatically with no CSV uploads, and our team monitors your Metrc account daily so discrepancies get fixed before an inspector finds them.[How to Reconcile Metrc Discrepancies at Your Dispensary →](https://getmeadow.com/blog/metrc-reconciliation-for-dispensaries)


### 2. Reliability and Uptime


Reliability is a platform's documented uptime and its record on 4/20 and other peak days, because an outage during your highest-volume hours is the single most expensive failure a POS can have. Ask for the uptime number in writing, a public status page you can check yourself, and references from stores your size that ran on the system last 4/20. Lag counts too: a register that makes customers wait a few seconds per screen costs sales on every busy shift.


### 3. Total Cost


Total cost is what you will pay in a year for everything you actually use: POS, eCommerce, delivery, loyalty, payments, and support. One flat monthly fee stays predictable; per-transaction fees grow as you do, and a low headline rate with a percentage cut often costs more at scale.


The cheapest system can also be the most expensive one to fix. A Metrc error or a tax miscalculation can cost more to untangle than the software costs in a year. Price the whole stack, including any subscriptions you would add for delivery, loyalty, or text marketing if the POS doesn't include them. (See our[cannabis POS pricing guide](https://getmeadow.com/blog/cannabis-pos-pricing) for what dispensaries actually pay in 2026.)


### 4. Speed on the Floor


Speed on the floor is how many taps a sale takes and how long it takes a new budtender to ring one alone. Slow transactions show up as a line out the door on your busiest night, and as labor hours every week after that. Ask how many clicks routine tasks take, and whether training is self-paced so new hires can learn before their first shift.


Fewer taps per sale keep the line moving at the counter.


### 5. All-in-One Scope


All-in-one scope means POS,[eCommerce](https://getmeadow.com/features/ecommerce) ,[delivery](https://getmeadow.com/features/cannabis-delivery) ,[loyalty](https://getmeadow.com/features/loyalty-and-rewards) , and payments run in one system on one inventory, so a sale in any channel updates stock everywhere. Every[integration](https://getmeadow.com/integrations) you add is a seam that can break, and every seam is a handoff your team has to remember. Three questions sort this out quickly:


- Does delivery support both hub-and-spoke and dynamic models, where drivers take new orders while already on the road?
- Do your Weedmaps and Leafly menus update automatically from POS inventory?
- Are loyalty rewards such as cash back, percent off, and free product built in?


### 6. Support Model


The support model is whether help is free and fast or billed per ticket, and who answers when you call. You will need help on a busy night. Message each vendor's support with a real question during your evaluation, time the reply, and read operator reviews for how support performs after the contract is signed.


### 7. Data Ownership


Data ownership is your right to export your sales, inventory, and customer data freely and take it with you if you leave. Ask for the export policy in writing, and ask who can sell or share your data. If the answer is fuzzy, that's the answer.

*Best for:* retailers in BioTrack or mixed-traceability markets.


*What sets it apart:* support for both Metrc and BioTrack, which matters if you operate in mixed-traceability markets.

### Treez

*Watch-outs:* longer onboarding and heavier configuration than a single-location store usually needs, with eCommerce and delivery billed as separate products. ### Cova


*Best for:* storefront-only retailers who don't need delivery.

## How to Choose: A Four-Step Framework


The fastest way to choose a dispensary POS is four steps: rule out on the deal-breakers, match the platform to your sales model, demo your real scenarios, and test support before you sign.


1. **Rule out on the deal-breakers first.**[Compliance automation](https://getmeadow.com/features/metrc-compliance) , uptime, and total cost. A low score on any one knocks a platform out, no matter how good the rest looks.
2. **Match the platform to your model.** Heavy delivery, a consumption lounge, multi-location, or a single store all push you toward different strengths.
3. **Demo with your real scenarios.** A 4/20 rush, a delivery run, a Metrc discrepancy, a return, and a same-day promo pushed to your online menu. Watch how the system handles your actual workflows and your tax setup.
4. **Check references and test support before you sign.** Message their support with a real question and time the reply. Ask operators your size what breaks, and check the vendor's status page for its record on recent peak days.

## Common Questions


### What's the best dispensary POS system in 2026?


The best dispensary POS system is the one that automates compliance, stays up on peak days, and fits your sales model. Meadow holds a 4.9 rating on G2 across 92 reviews as of November 2026, with 99.999% uptime since 2014 and one platform spanning in-store, delivery, and eCommerce. It's Metrc-only and live in six states (CA, MI, MA, NY, NJ, MN), so confirm it serves your market.


### How do I compare cannabis POS systems?


Score each platform on seven criteria: compliance automation, uptime, total cost, speed on the floor, all-in-one scope, support, and data ownership. Treat compliance, uptime, and total cost as deal-breakers, and rule out any platform that fails one of them before you compare features.


### What features should a dispensary POS system have?


A dispensary POS system should have automated track-and-trace reporting, accurate inventory with cycle counts, in-store, pickup, and delivery sales from one inventory, built-in loyalty, automatic menu sync with marketplaces like Weedmaps and Leafly, and reporting down to the product and brand. It should also calculate state excise, local, and sales taxes correctly for every order type.


### Which dispensary POS is best for multiple locations?


For multi-location dispensaries, look for real-time multi-store inventory, fast staff training, and consistent reporting across stores. Off the Charts runs over 40 stores on Meadow using its cycle counts and Meadow Mastery training program.


### What's the most important feature in a cannabis POS?


Automatic compliance reporting paired with reliable uptime. Everything else is secondary if the system fails an audit or goes down at peak, because both failures cost money the same day they happen.


### How much does a dispensary POS cost?


Dispensary POS pricing depends on the model. Flat-fee platforms charge one predictable monthly rate per location; others add per-transaction fees or revenue share that grow with your sales. Compare the total annual cost of everything you will actually use. (See our[cannabis POS pricing guide](https://getmeadow.com/blog/cannabis-pos-pricing) .)
